# Are GSE309890 and GDS309890 the same record?

## Abstract

A user asked whether the GEO accessions GSE309890 and GDS309890 denote the same object. The two prefixes name different GEO entry types held in the same Entrez `gds` index: GSE is a submitter-deposited Series, GDS is an NCBI-curated DataSet. Accession-to-UID resolution (`geo_resolve_accession`) confirmed the two strings map to different Entrez UIDs, 200309890 for GSE309890 and 309890 for GDS309890, under GEO's rule that a GSE takes a leading type digit of 2 and a GDS takes none. Retrieval of each UID (`geo_series`) returned a populated record for GSE309890 — an *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655 RNA-seq Series of 6 samples on platform GPL24659, BioProject PRJNA1363958, public 2026/02/01, with one supplementary FPKM file of 510K — and an empty record with no accession, no title and no FTP directory for UID 309890, indicating GDS309890 does not exist. A search of the `gds` entry type returned 4,348 curated DataSets in total, so no GDS accession approaches 309890. A real curated DataSet, GDS5163 (6 samples, GPL3154, PMID 24803433), was retrieved for contrast. The answer is that the two accessions are not the same thing, and only one of them exists. This matters because a `gds` free-text search for a GEO accession returns related records rather than errors, so a mistyped prefix can silently return a plausible but wrong record.

## I. Introduction

**Background.** GEO stores four kinds of record in a single Entrez database named `gds`: Series (GSE), Platform (GPL), Sample (GSM), and curated DataSet (GDS). A Series is what a submitter deposits — a group of samples forming one study. A curated DataSet is an NCBI-assembled, value-normalised collection built on top of Series data; curation of new GDS records has been largely inactive, and the GDS numbering space is small. Because all four types share one index, the prefix is the only thing distinguishing them in a query.

**Literature Review.** GSE309890 carries no linked PubMed record; the tool reported "No PubMed record is linked to this GEO record," which it noted typically means unpublished or not-yet-indexed and never means the study has no data. The contrast record GDS5163 carries one linked PubMed identifier, PMID 24803433, retrieved as part of its summary. No abstracts were fetched.

**Knowledge Gap.** Before the query it was unresolved whether the numeric part of an accession identifies a record independently of its prefix, and whether a GDS record bearing the number 309890 exists at all.

**Objective & Hypothesis.** Objective: determine whether GSE309890 and GDS309890 resolve to the same GEO record. Testable expectation: if the prefix is semantically meaningful, the two strings resolve to different Entrez UIDs and at most one retrieves a populated record.

## II. Materials and Methods

**Study Design.** The question is one of identifier semantics, so it was routed entirely to NCBI GEO through the dedicated GEO tools rather than to a federated search. Accession resolution was done first because the UID mapping is arithmetic and costs no NCBI request; record retrieval followed to test whether each computed UID corresponds to a real record. A known-good GDS and a total GDS count were added to establish whether GDS309890 falls inside the populated range.

**Materials.**
- NCBI GEO accession-to-UID mapping, via `geo_resolve_accession`.
- NCBI GEO record retrieval (Entrez `esummary` on db `gds`), via `geo_series`.
- NCBI GEO record search (Entrez `esearch` on db `gds`), via `geo_search`.

**Procedures.**
1. `geo_resolve_accession(accessions="GSE309890 GDS309890")`.
2. `geo_series(accession="GSE309890")` — default `list_files=true`, so the FTP supplementary directory was listed.
3. `geo_series(accession="GDS309890")` — default `list_files=true`.
4. `geo_series(accession="GDS5163", list_files=false)` — a control, a GDS known to the tool documentation.
5. `geo_search(entry_type="gds", term="all[sb]", max_results=1)` — to obtain the total number of curated DataSets.

**Statistical Analysis.** No statistics were computed. The UIDs are deterministic transformations of the accession, reported by the resolver as "UID = type digit + accession number padded to 8 digits. GPL=1, GSE=2, GSM=3, and GDS takes no digit at all." Existence was judged from whether the `esummary` response carried a non-empty `accession` and `entry_type`. The count of 4,348 is the `total_count` field of the `esearch` response for the query `(all[sb]) AND "gds"[Filter]`, not a page size; the tool flagged that NCBI rewrote the term before running it.

## III. Results

**Data Presentation.**

**Table 1. Resolution and retrieval of the two queried accessions.**

| Accession | Entrez UID | Entry type | Record returned | FTP directory registered |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GSE309890 | 200309890 | GSE (Series) | Populated | Yes, with 1 supplementary file |
| GDS309890 | 309890 | GDS (curated DataSet) | Empty (no accession, no title, no type) | No; soft directory does not exist |

**Table 2. Content of the records retrieved.**

| Field | GSE309890 | GDS309890 | GDS5163 (control) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Entry type label | Series | — | curated DataSet |
| Title | Antidepressant sertraline biases resistance emergence via stress-driven rewiring of the pentose phosphate pathway: tktA enables metabolic rollback | — | Hydrogen peroxide-scavenging enzymes AhpCF, KatE and KatG deficiency |
| Taxon | Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655 | — | Escherichia coli; Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655 |
| Experiment type | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing | — | Expression profiling by array |
| Platform | GPL24659 | — | GPL3154 |
| Sample count | 6 | — | 6 |
| BioProject | PRJNA1363958 | — | PRJNA242527 |
| Date public | 2026/02/01 | — | 2014/04/02 |
| Linked PubMed IDs | 0 | — | 1 (24803433) |
| Supplementary files | 1 CSV, GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz, 510K, modified 2025-11-14 | 0 | CEL |

**Findings.**

GSE309890 and GDS309890 resolve to two different Entrez UIDs, 200309890 and 309890 respectively. They are not the same record.

GSE309890 exists. It is a Series of 6 samples (GSM9284457–GSM9284462: three controls, three 40-day adaptive-evolution replicates) in *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655, profiled by high-throughput sequencing on GPL24659, registered under BioProject PRJNA1363958, public 2026/02/01, with one supplementary FPKM CSV of 510K.

GDS309890 does not exist. The `esummary` call on UID 309890 returned a record with an empty accession, empty entry type, empty title and empty taxon, and the FTP soft directory for that accession was reported absent.

The `gds` entry type holds 4,348 curated DataSets in total. The number 309890 lies far outside that range, which is consistent with the empty retrieval.

A real curated DataSet, GDS5163, returned a fully populated record on the same tool path, confirming the empty GDS309890 result reflects absence of the record rather than failure of the method.

## IV. Discussion

**Interpretation.** The objective is met and the expectation holds. The prefix is not decorative: it selects the entry type and changes the Entrez UID, so the same digits under two prefixes address two different slots in the index. Of the two slots, only the GSE one is occupied. Anyone holding the string "GDS309890" is holding a malformed accession, almost certainly a GSE with the prefix swapped.

**Context.** The contrast between GDS5163 and GDS309890 locates the boundary. GDS accessions run into the low thousands and the total population is 4,348; GSE accessions have passed 309,000. A six-digit number after a GDS prefix is therefore self-evidently out of range, independent of any lookup. The retrieved GSE309890 record is itself a coherent study — sertraline-driven adaptive evolution in *E. coli* — with data files present on the FTP tree, so the underlying object the user is likely after is available.

**Limitations.** The resolver computes UIDs arithmetically and does not verify existence, so a resolved UID is not evidence that a record exists; only the retrieval step establishes that. The `geo_search` total of 4,348 came from a query NCBI rewrote before running, as the tool flagged, so it should be read as the count for the rewritten query. The GEO API returns metadata only: the FPKM values for GSE309890 exist solely in the supplementary file on the FTP tree and were not downloaded or inspected here. The absence of a linked PubMed record for GSE309890 does not establish that the study is unpublished. These data cannot establish why the GDS prefix was used, nor whether GEO ever intends to curate this Series into a GDS.

**Conclusion & Future Directions.** GSE309890 and GDS309890 are not the same thing. GSE309890 is a real *E. coli* RNA-seq Series; GDS309890 is not a record in GEO. The next query worth running is a download of `GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz` from the Series FTP directory, since the processed expression values live only there, and a lookup of BioProject PRJNA1363958 in SRA to reach the raw reads behind the six samples.

## References

[1] NCBI GEO, accession-to-UID resolution for GSE309890 and GDS309890 (`geo_resolve_accession`). GEO pages: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890 and https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GDS309890

[2] NCBI GEO Series GSE309890 record, Entrez esummary db=gds id=200309890 (`geo_series`). https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890 ; API: https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esummary.fcgi

[3] NCBI GEO FTP directory for GSE309890. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/

[4] NCBI GEO supplementary file GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz (510K, 2025-11-14). https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz

[5] NCBI GEO, empty retrieval for UID 309890, Entrez esummary db=gds (`geo_series`); soft directory reported absent. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/datasets/GDS309nnn/GDS309890/soft/

[6] NCBI GEO curated DataSet GDS5163, Entrez esummary db=gds id=5163 (`geo_series`). https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GDS5163 ; FTP: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/datasets/GDS5nnn/GDS5163/

[7] NCBI PubMed, PMID 24803433, linked from GDS5163 (identifier only; abstract not retrieved).

[8] NCBI GEO, count of curated DataSets, Entrez esearch db=gds term=`(all[sb]) AND "gds"[Filter]` (`geo_search`), total_count 4348. https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi

[9] NCBI GEO curated DataSet GDS6063, returned as the first hit of the count query. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/datasets/GDS6nnn/GDS6063/

## Acknowledgments

Records were provided by the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus and the NCBI Entrez E-utilities, National Center for Biotechnology Information, U.S. National Library of Medicine. The GSE309890 data were deposited by the submitting authors of that Series under BioProject PRJNA1363958; the GDS5163 data by the submitters of BioProject PRJNA242527.
